subject.title: Feature Request: Image batching / media group buffering at gateway layer

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic media-aware inbound batching contract for channels without native media group IDs, or should media batching remain channel/plugin-specific?
rationale: The remaining request changes public config/API surface, latency defaults, session grouping, and media attachment semantics across channel boundaries; repository policy requires maintainer direction before adding that kind of product surface.

options.title: Design generic media batching contract
options.body: Define a typed channel/gateway batching seam with explicit keys, media preservation, flush semantics, command bypass rules, defaults, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep channel-specific fixes only
options.body: Treat Telegram as already solved and handle WhatsApp/LINE-style cases in each plugin without creating a new shared gateway contract.

options.title: Defer for more live evidence
options.body: Keep the issue open but require concrete non-Telegram reproduction and target UX proof before choosing a core API.

recommendation.title: Design generic media batching contract
recommendation.body: Define a typed channel/gateway batching seam with explicit keys, media preservation, flush semantics, command bypass rules, defaults, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared debounce-policy refactor is the central current boundary that maintainers would need to expand or deliberately leave text-only.
